en: The Discourse on the Four Assemblies 1. The Blessed One, the Bodhisattva, while dwelling at Uruvilvā on the bank of the river Nairañjanā at the foot of the Bodhi tree, remained constantly engaged, alert, and devoted to the practice of yoga in the cultivation of the factors conducive to awakening (bodhipākṣika-dharma).

2. During the first watch of the night, he directed his mind toward the supernormal knowledge (abhijñā) that realizes the domain of psychic power (ṛddhiviṣaya), and he experienced various kinds of psychic power.
3. That is to say: having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one;
he appears and disappears, experiencing this through his knowledge and vision.

He passes through walls, through mountains, and through enclosures without being obstructed by his body, just as if in open space; he performs the act of emerging and submerging within the earth just as if in water;
he moves through water with his body without being obstructed, just as if on the earth;
and he travels cross-legged through the sky just like a winged bird.
Even these two, the moon and the sun, so powerful and so majestic, he wipes and polishes with his hand; even as far as the Brahma-world, he exercises mastery over them with his body.

Thus the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva, dwelling at Uruvilvā on the bank of the river Nairañjanā at the foot of the Bodhi tree—practicing continuously, alert, and devoted to the application of cultivation in the factors conducive to enlightenment—experienced various kinds of supernormal powers during the first watch of the night.
5. Then the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva, while dwelling at Uruvilvā—as previously described—remained devotedly engaged [in spiritual practice].
6. During the first watch of the night, he directed his mind toward the supernormal knowledge that realizes the recollection of former existences; he recollected his manifold former existences: 7.
namely, one birth, two, three, four, and even many eons of world-dissolution and evolution.

8. Thus the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva, dwelling at Uruvilvā on the bank of the river Nairañjanā at the foot of the Bodhi tree, practicing with constancy, being vigilant, and devoted to the application of cultivation toward the factors conducive to awakening, recalled his former births during the first watch of the night. 9. Then the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva, dwelling at Uruvilvā—as previously described—dwelt thus devoted until the end.

10. During the middle watch of the night, he directed his mind toward the higher knowledge that realizes the superknowledge of the divine ear. With the purified divine ear, which transcends that of humans, he heard both kinds of sounds—those of humans, whether far or near.

11. Thus, while dwelling at Uruvilvā on the bank of the Nairañjanā River at the foot of the Bodhi tree, the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva, being constant and vigilant, applied himself to the cultivation of the factors conducive to awakening.
Dwelling devotedly, during the middle watch of the night, he experiences the knowledge of the divine ear.
12. Then the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva, dwelling at Uruvilvā—as previously described—dwelt devotedly.
13. During the middle watch of the night, he directed his mind toward the science that realizes the knowledge of the divine eye.
14. With the divine eye, purified and surpassing that of humans, he sees beings passing away and being reborn—beings who are beautiful and ugly, lowly and exalted;
he understands, as it truly is, how beings fare according to their karma, whether they go to a good destination or a bad destination.

15. Thus, these worthy beings, possessed of misconduct of body, possessed of misconduct of speech and mind, revilers of the noble ones, holding wrong views, because of their undertaking of actions and dharmas based on wrong view, for that cause and for that condition...

After the breaking up of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a state of ruin, in the hells. On the other hand, these worthy beings, endowed with good conduct of body, endowed with good conduct of speech and mind, not revilers of the noble ones, possessing right view, through the cause of undertaking actions and dharmas based on right view— by that cause and by that condition— after the breaking up of the body, are reborn in a happy destination, in a heavenly world, among the gods.

17. Thus the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva, while dwelling at Urubilvā on the bank of the river Nairañjanā at the foot of the Bodhi tree, practicing with constancy, wise, and devoted to the application of cultivation regarding the factors conducive to awakening, experienced the knowledge of the divine eye during the middle watch of the night.
18. Then the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva, while dwelling at Urubilvā—as previously described—dwelt devotedly [to the practice].

19. During the final watch of the night, he directs his mind toward the superknowledge that realizes the knowledge of the mental dispositions of others (*cetaḥparyāyajñāna-sākṣātkriyā-abhijñā*). 20. He understands, as they truly are, the thoughts and reflections, the mental and intellectual states, of other beings and other persons;
he understands, as it truly is, a mind possessed of passion as "a mind possessed of passion."

He understands as it really is a mind free from lust as "a mind free from lust"; he understands as it really is a mind with hatred as "with hatred," a mind free from hatred as "free from hatred," a deluded mind as "deluded," a mind free from delusion as "free from delusion," a distracted mind as "distracted," a concentrated mind as "concentrated," a sunken mind as "sunken," an uplifted mind as "uplifted," an agitated mind as "agitated," an unagitated mind as "unagitated," an unpacified mind as "unpacified," a pacified mind as "pacified," a composed mind as "composed," an uncomposed mind as "uncomposed," an uncultivated mind as "uncultivated," a cultivated mind as "cultivated," and an unliberated mind as "an unliberated mind. He understands it as it really is.

21. Thus the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva, dwelling at Uruvilvā on the bank of the river Nairañjanā at the foot of the Bodhi tree, practicing with constancy, wise, and devoted to the application of cultivation regarding the factors conducive to awakening, experienced the knowledge of the penetration of others' minds during the last watch of the night.
22. Then the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva, dwelling at Uruvilvā—as previously described—dwelt devotedly [to the practice] until that point.

23. During the final watch of the night, he directs his mind toward the superknowledge that realizes the knowledge of the destruction of the outflows (*āsravakṣayajñānasākṣikriyā*). 24. He understands, as it truly is, "This is the noble truth of suffering," and "This is the origin of suffering."
"This is the cessation of suffering;
this is the noble truth of the practice leading to the cessation of suffering"—thus he understands it as it truly is.
For him who knows thus and sees thus, the mind is liberated from the influx of sensual desire.
The mind is liberated from the outflow of existence and from the outflow of ignorance.

For one who is liberated, the knowledge and vision arises: "I am liberated. [He knows: "Birth is exhausted for me; the holy life has been lived; what was to be done has been accomplished; I know no further state of existence beyond this."

25. Thus the Blessed One, dwelling at Uruvilvā on the bank of the river Nairañjanā at the foot of the Bodhi tree, having accomplished his purpose and performed what was to be done, entered the fire-element as one perfectly awakened.
